home-remodeling.local_heading: Remodeling on an island that runs by ferry
intro_paragraphs: Fisher Island is condominium living nearly wall to wall: Mediterranean-leaning mid-rises from the island's first wave of development, like Bayside Village, Seaside Village, and Oceanside, plus newer towers such as Palazzo Del Sol and Palazzo Della Luna. The late-1980s residences are where the serious remodeling happens — interiors pushing forty, original plumbing and electrical, and compartmentalized floor plans drawn for a different era of entertaining. Owners here rarely settle for a refresh. They gut to the shell, open the layout toward the water, replace every system, and refinish to the standard the address quietly demands.

Because Fisher Island is unincorporated Miami-Dade County, building permits run through the county's building department, Regulatory and Economic Resources, rather than a city hall. That is only the first gate. The Fisher Island Community Association registers and approves contractors, your building's own association reviews the alteration, insurance certificates get verified, and crews and materials move on scheduled contractor access rather than the resident ferry. Add Miami-Dade product approvals for impact windows in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, plus the milestone-inspection era now surrounding the island's late-1980s buildings, and a remodel here rewards a contractor who reads paperwork as fluently as plans.

Fisher Island is where PGX Builders Group's preparation shows: more than 20 years building in South Florida, 150+ remodels and additions delivered. We put a fixed scope in writing before demolition, supervise the site daily, and protect corridors, elevators, and finishes the way building managers expect. Every delivery is sequenced, because a missing fitting on this island costs half a day, not a quick drive. One licensed and insured team — Lic. CGC1539072 — carries your project from estimate through warranty, in person, on the island.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: Fisher Island sits in unincorporated Miami-Dade County, so permits come from the county building department rather than any city. That is one of three approvals a remodel typically needs: the county permit, your condominium association's sign-off on the alteration, and contractor registration with the Fisher Island Community Association. We run all three tracks in parallel so the approvals overlap instead of stacking end to end.

faqs.q: How do construction crews and materials actually reach the island?
faqs.a: Not on the resident ferry. Registered contractors move crews, vehicles, and materials through the island's scheduled contractor access, and bulk materials travel by barge. There is no hardware store on Fisher Island, so we plan deliveries the way a ship provisions: everything ordered, staged, and confirmed before it crosses. It is the single biggest difference between contractors who work here regularly and those who try it once.

faqs.q: How long does a full remodel take on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: Longer than the same scope on the mainland, and anyone who says otherwise has not worked here. County permitting, association review, contractor registration, and ferry-and-barge logistics each add real time. A full-unit renovation is a months-long project, not a season of weekends. What we control is predictability: a written schedule tied to a fixed scope, daily supervision, and deliveries sequenced so the job never sits idle waiting on a faucet.

faqs.q: Do milestone inspections affect renovation plans in my building?
faqs.a: They can, in useful ways. Most of Fisher Island's buildings date to the late 1980s and early 1990s, which puts them squarely in Florida's milestone structural inspection cycle. If your association has inspection or repair work planned, we coordinate scope and scheduling with the building's engineer so your renovation is not opened twice. Renovating with the milestone calendar in view is cheaper than discovering it mid-project.

faqs.q: What does a whole-unit remodel cost on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: More than the identical scope would cost across the bay, honestly — island logistics, association requirements, and the level of finish owners here expect all carry real cost. We do not publish square-foot prices because they mislead in both directions. What we offer instead is a fixed written scope with transparent pricing before work begins, so the number you approve is the number you pay, barring changes you direct.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling for Fisher Island Residences, Miami FL
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchens for Fisher Island condos and villas — cabinetry, stone, and lighting, with every slab scheduled onto the barge. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom kitchens for Fisher Island condos and villas — cabinetry, stone, and lighting installed by a licensed, insured Miami-Dade contractor who schedules the barge as carefully as the backsplash.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Kitchens for the far side of Government Cut
intro_paragraphs: On Fisher Island, the kitchen is usually the first room to betray a residence's age. Units at Bayside Village, Seaside Village, and Oceanside came with the enclosed, galley-leaning kitchens of the late 1980s — fine for caterers, less fine for owners who actually cook facing the water. The prevailing move is a full rebuild: walls opened toward the living area where structure allows, a stone island where a peninsula once was, custom cabinetry to the ceiling, and appliances repositioned around how the household really runs. Even newer residences at Palazzo Del Sol get personalized, because developer-spec is a starting point here, not a destination.

Kitchen work on the island is permitted through Miami-Dade County — Fisher Island is unincorporated, so the county building department reviews the plumbing, electrical, and structural portions of the job. Your condominium association reviews it too, and association rules often limit where wet lines can move relative to the unit below. The Fisher Island Community Association separately registers every contractor and subcontractor before anyone boards. None of this is a problem; it is simply a sequence, and we have learned to run the county, the building, and the island approvals at the same time rather than one after another.

The logistics are where a Fisher Island kitchen is won or lost. A twelve-foot quartzite slab cannot be re-cut at the marina, so we template precisely, inspect fabrication on the mainland, and schedule the crossing only when the piece is right. Cabinetry arrives protected and sequenced, corridors are shielded, and a PGX supervisor is on site daily — the same accountable team, licensed under CGC1539072, from the first written estimate to the warranty visit. That is how a kitchen gets built beautifully in a place where you cannot send someone out for parts.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in a Fisher Island condo?
faqs.a: Yes. Fisher Island is unincorporated Miami-Dade County, so the county issues the permit, and any electrical, plumbing, or wall changes will require one. Your building's association must also approve the alteration, and the Fisher Island Community Association must register the contractor before work starts. Unpermitted kitchen work surfaces at resale and in association records, so doing it properly is not just legal — it protects the unit's value.

faqs.q: Can I move my kitchen to a different part of the unit?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The structure usually cooperates; the rules are the variable. Many associations limit relocating water and drain lines over a neighbor's living space, and drain routing in a mid-rise slab has real constraints. We review the building's alteration policy and the as-built conditions before you fall in love with a floor plan, and we tell you plainly what is achievable, what is negotiable, and what is not worth the fight.

faqs.q: How do appliances and stone get to Fisher Island?
faqs.a: By water, on a schedule. Contractor materials cross by barge and scheduled contractor access, not the resident ferry, which means a delivery missed is a day lost. We consolidate orders, receive and inspect everything on the mainland first, and send nothing across until it is confirmed complete and undamaged. Your Sub-Zero does not ride over twice.

faqs.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take on the island?
faqs.a: Plan on the approvals taking as long as the construction. County permitting, association review, and contractor registration happen before demolition; the build itself is typically a matter of weeks once cabinetry and stone are in hand. The honest schedule risk is fabrication lead time, which is why we order long-lead items the day the scope is signed and stage the work so your residence is never torn open and waiting.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a high-end kitchen here?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry, natural stone, and appliance-grade electrical work carry the same premium here they do anywhere in Miami's luxury market — island logistics add a real but modest layer on top. We will not quote a number sight unseen, because unit conditions vary enormously between a 1988 tower and a 2019 one. What you get from PGX is a fixed written price tied to a complete specification, before demolition, with no allowance games.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring us the wish list. We will measure, advise on what the building allows, and put a real price on it — in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary baths, frameless showers, and freestanding tubs for Fisher Island residences — permitted through Miami-Dade County, waterproofed like it matters, and supervised daily by one licensed, insured team.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Salt air raises the stakes on waterproofing
intro_paragraphs: The bathrooms are usually the most dated rooms left on Fisher Island. Residences at Seaside Villas, Bayside Village, and Villa del Mare were finished when jetted corner tubs and brass fittings were the height of ambition, and owners have been quietly replacing them ever since. The current standard is a true primary suite: a curbless frameless shower, a freestanding tub set against the light, book-matched stone, warm concealed lighting, and fittings chosen to survive salt air. It is precision work in a compact space, which is exactly why it rewards a builder who does it constantly.

Bathroom renovations here are permitted through Miami-Dade County, because Fisher Island is unincorporated — plumbing, electrical, and any wall changes go through county review and inspection. The building layer matters just as much: associations typically require approved waterproofing details, licensed and insured trades, scheduled water shutdowns coordinated with management, and proof that the contractor is registered with the Fisher Island Community Association. In a building where your shower pan sits above a neighbor's dressing room, none of that is bureaucracy. It is the difference between a renovation and a future insurance claim.

PGX builds bathrooms the unglamorous way first: full waterproofing membranes, flood-tested pans, sealed penetrations, and photographs of all of it before a single tile goes on. Then the glamorous part — stone, glass, brass or nickel, lighting that flatters at 7 a.m. Our crews work clean in occupied buildings, protect the corridor from door to door, and answer to a supervisor who is on the island daily. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, licensed and insured under CGC1539072, and a written fixed scope before demolition: that is the whole pitch.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a bathroom remodel on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: Yes, for anything beyond paint and accessories. Fisher Island is unincorporated Miami-Dade County, so plumbing, electrical, and layout changes are permitted and inspected by the county building department. Your association will also require approval of the alteration and evidence of contractor registration with the Fisher Island Community Association. We prepare and track all of it — it is routine for us, and it should never become homework for you.

faqs.q: How do you protect the unit below mine?
faqs.a: With redundancy. Every shower and wet area gets a continuous waterproofing membrane, a flood-tested pan, and sealed penetrations, all photographed before tile conceals them. Water shutdowns are scheduled with building management, supply connections are pressure-checked, and we leave documentation your association can keep on file. High-rise water damage travels down, and the only acceptable amount of it is none.

faqs.q: Can I relocate the toilet or shower in my condo bathroom?
faqs.a: Within limits. Drain locations in a condominium slab are the governing constraint, and associations often restrict moving wet areas over a neighbor's dry space. Some relocations are straightforward, some need creative routing, and a few are genuinely not worth it. We assess the as-built plumbing before design gets ambitious, so the layout you approve is one the building can actually accept.

faqs.q: How disruptive is a bathroom renovation in an occupied Fisher Island residence?
faqs.a: Less than you fear, if it is run properly. We contain dust at the room, protect floors from the front door in, work within the building's permitted hours, and remove debris on the contractor schedule rather than letting it age in a hallway. Many owners stay in residence for a single-bath project; for full primary suites, some choose to time the work around travel. Either way, the site is left clean daily.

faqs.q: What does a primary bath renovation cost at this level?
faqs.a: A properly built primary suite with stone, frameless glass, and relocated fixtures is a significant investment — comfortably into five figures and often well beyond, depending on scope and materials. Island logistics add a measured premium. We would rather show you exactly where the money goes: every PGX proposal is a fixed, itemized scope in writing, so you compare selections, not mystery allowances.

home-additions.title: Home Additions & Unit Combinations on Fisher Island, FL
home-additions.meta_description: Adding space on Fisher Island means combining residences. Engineered openings, Miami-Dade permits, association approvals — PGX Builders, (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Fisher Island has no spare lots, so PGX adds space the island way — combining adjacent residences, opening structure between them, and permitting every inch through Miami-Dade County under daily licensed supervision.
home-additions.local_heading: Adding space where the land ran out
intro_paragraphs: On an island of condominiums, adding square footage means acquiring it next door. The established Fisher Island move is the unit combination: two residences at Oceanside, Bayside Village, or one of the Palazzo buildings joined into a single great flat, with an engineered opening where a demising wall stood, kitchens consolidated, and the second entry absorbed. Owners also rework the island's villa-style residences at Seaside Villas, capturing hallways, closets, and awkward 1980s planning to make the footprint live larger than its deed suggests.

Combining units is structural work, and the approvals treat it that way. Fisher Island is unincorporated, so plans, engineering, and inspections run through Miami-Dade County's building department, with a Florida-licensed engineer signing the opening in what is often a load-bearing or fire-rated demising wall. Your association must approve the combination under its governing documents, and the Fisher Island Community Association registers the contractor before mobilization. Buildings dating to the late 1980s are also in Florida's milestone-inspection cycle, which makes clean structural documentation more valuable than ever. We assemble that package — architect, engineer, association, county — as one coordinated submission.

We start with feasibility, not enthusiasm. Before you buy the unit next door, PGX can review the demising wall construction, the mechanical systems that will need to merge, and the association's appetite for combinations, then tell you in writing what the project honestly involves. From there it is our standard discipline: a fixed scope, one accountable licensed team under CGC1539072, daily on-island supervision, and finish protection worthy of the buildings we work in. More than 20 years in South Florida taught us that the best additions are the ones engineered before they are imagined finished.

faqs.q: Can I combine two condo units on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: Frequently, yes — combinations are an established practice in the island's buildings. What it takes: your association's approval under its governing documents, engineering for the opening in the shared wall, Miami-Dade County permits and inspections, and contractor registration with the Fisher Island Community Association. The wall between units may be load-bearing or fire-rated, so the engineering is real, not a formality. We can assess a specific pair of units before you commit to buying the second one.

faqs.q: Can I enclose my terrace or balcony to gain interior space?
faqs.a: Treat it as a maybe with a heavy burden of proof. Balconies and their railings are usually common elements under association control, and enclosure raises structural, waterproofing, and High-Velocity Hurricane Zone glazing questions along with county permitting. Some associations prohibit it outright; others have a defined process. We will read your building's documents and give you a straight answer before anyone draws a rendering.

faqs.q: Could I build a conventional addition or second story here?
faqs.a: For nearly every Fisher Island property, no — the housing is condominium in form, the land belongs to the community, and expanding a building's envelope is not on the table for an individual owner. That is not a dead end; it is why combinations and deep interior re-planning are the island's version of an addition. When owners want true detached-home expansion, it usually means a different address, and we will say so plainly.

faqs.q: How long does a unit combination take from decision to done?
faqs.a: The paperwork phase is measured in months — association review, engineering, county permitting, and island contractor registration all precede demolition. Construction on a well-planned combination then moves steadily, since most of the work is interior. The variable that wrecks schedules is discovering conditions mid-project, which is why we open, scan, and verify the shared wall and systems early. Expect a real timeline in writing from us, not a hopeful one.

faqs.q: Is combining units worth it financially on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: We build, we do not give investment advice — but we can tell you what owners weigh. Large single-floor residences are scarce on the island, and combining is often the only way to create one without leaving. Against that, you are funding two acquisitions plus structural work and finishes at island logistics pricing. Our role is making the construction side knowable: a fixed written scope, so the decision rests on real numbers.

outdoor-living.h1: Outdoor rooms that shrug off salt air
outdoor-living.hero_sub: PGX renovates Fisher Island terraces, villa patios, and penthouse decks — waterproofed, engineered for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, permitted through Miami-Dade County, and finished to association standards under daily supervision.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Salt air is the client too
intro_paragraphs: Outdoor life on Fisher Island happens on terraces, loggias, and villa patios with some of the best sightlines in Miami — ships gliding through Government Cut on one side, the marina and Atlantic horizon on others. Much of that outdoor space is original to buildings finished decades ago, and it reads that way: worn decking, dated finishes, a grill cart standing in for a summer kitchen. Owners across the island, from Seaside Villas to the Palazzo buildings, are rebuilding these into genuine outdoor rooms, with stone or porcelain underfoot, weatherproof cabinetry and refrigeration, and lighting that makes the terrace the favorite room by sunset.

Exterior work carries the island's full stack of oversight. Permits go through Miami-Dade County, since Fisher Island is unincorporated, and anything glazed or structural must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements with county product approvals. Terraces and balconies are typically common elements or under association aesthetic control, so your building approves materials, colors, and details before the county sees a plan, and Florida's structural-inspection era has associations rightly attentive to balcony waterproofing. The Fisher Island Community Association registers contractors and governs how crews and materials move. It is a long list of gates, and knowing the order they open in is most of the schedule.

Building outdoors here is a materials exam first and a construction project second. Salt air corrodes ordinary hardware, UV bleaches ordinary finishes, and any new decking over occupied space below is really a waterproofing project wearing nice stone. PGX specifies marine-grade fasteners, tested membranes, and finishes that will still look intentional in year ten, then installs them under daily supervision with the discretion an island of private residences expects. Fixed written scope, licensed and insured under CGC1539072, and one team accountable from the first site walk to the warranty call. The view was always good; the terrace should deserve it.

faqs.q: Can I renovate my balcony or terrace, or does it belong to the association?
faqs.a: Usually both, in different layers. In most Fisher Island buildings the structural slab, railings, and exterior appearance are common elements under association control, while the surfaces and improvements within your space are yours to renovate with approval. That split is defined in your building's declaration, and it decides what you may change and who pays for what. We read those documents before designing, and we build to whatever line they draw.

faqs.q: Can I add a summer kitchen or a gas grill on Fisher Island?
faqs.a: It depends on your building. Many associations restrict open flame or gas on balconies — a common rule in Florida high-rises — while villa patios often have more latitude. Electric grills, weatherproof cabinetry, refrigeration, and sinks are achievable far more often. We confirm the rules for your specific building first, then design a summer kitchen the association can approve and the county can permit, rather than the other way around.

faqs.q: Do outdoor projects on Fisher Island need permits?
faqs.a: Most do. The island is unincorporated Miami-Dade County, so the county permits electrical, plumbing, structural, and glazing work outdoors just as it does inside — and impact doors or anything wind-loaded needs products approved for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. Add your association's architectural approval and the island's contractor registration, and even a modest terrace project has a paper trail. We manage it as part of the job, not as an extra.

faqs.q: What materials actually last outdoors this close to the ocean?
faqs.a: Porcelain pavers and dense stone underfoot, marine-grade stainless hardware, powder-coated or anodized aluminum, teak that is allowed to silver, and lighting rated for coastal exposure. What fails is ordinary steel, bargain fixtures, and any coating applied over skipped prep. We have twenty-plus years of watching South Florida weather grade our industry's homework, and we specify accordingly — it costs somewhat more on day one and far less by year five.

faqs.q: How does exterior work coordinate with my building's inspections and repairs?
faqs.a: Closely, if it is planned well. Buildings from the island's original development period are in Florida's milestone-inspection cycle, and associations frequently schedule balcony, railing, or waterproofing repairs as a result. If your terrace renovation is coming, we talk to management first: sequencing your project with the building's work avoids paying to finish a surface the association later opens. Sometimes the answer is wait six months; we would rather tell you that now.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: An island the county still permits
intro_paragraphs: Fisher Island is 216 acres of condominium residences, villas and townhomes, and almost none of it is still original. The late-1980s and early-1990s buildings, Bayside Village, Seaside Village and Oceanside among them, have had kitchens gutted, walls moved, air handlers swapped and glazing replaced, sometimes twice. Palazzo Del Sol and Palazzo Della Luna were customized almost as soon as they were handed over. In Miami-Dade all of that is permit work: electrical, plumbing, mechanical, windows, doors, anything structural. Each round should have left a permit opened, inspected and closed. Plenty left one that was only opened.

Fisher Island is unincorporated Miami-Dade County: no village hall, no city architectural board. Permits are filed with the county's Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources. What replaces municipal design review here is private — contractor registration with the Fisher Island Community Association, your building's approval of the alteration, insurance certificates, and scheduled contractor access rather than the resident ferry. This is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so windows, doors and roofing need a valid Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance on file. The island's older buildings now sit inside the county recertification cycle everyone still calls the forty-year, alongside Florida's milestone inspections for condominium buildings three stories and taller.

PGX Builders Group has been building in South Florida for more than twenty years, with 150+ remodels and additions delivered and every one of them permitted and inspected. On a Fisher Island compliance job that means pulling the county record before we promise anything, coordinating the engineer or architect the file needs, answering plan review comments ourselves, and calling each inspection only when the work is genuinely ready. A second trip for an inspector here is a boat crossing, not a drive. Lic. CGC1539072 owns the file from first application to final sign-off. We cannot make a requirement disappear. We can make sure it never surprises you.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: What we handle, filing to sign-off
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Some owners call before the drawings exist. Others call because a title company found something two weeks before closing. Both are normal here, and both are fixable.

scope_items.name: Open permits, traced and closed
scope_items.desc: Old and expired permits pulled from county records, taken over under our license, corrected where the work fails, re-inspected and signed off before your closing date.

scope_items.name: County filings and plan review
scope_items.desc: Drawings, product data and applications assembled and submitted to Miami-Dade, with review comments answered by us rather than forwarded to you as a PDF.

scope_items.name: Product approvals, unit by unit
scope_items.desc: Windows, doors and roofing specified with a current Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance, then installed to the detail that approval actually covers, not an approximation of it.

scope_items.name: Inspections, called once
scope_items.desc: Each phase scheduled when it is genuinely ready, so an inspector's first crossing to the island is also the only one your calendar has to absorb.

scope_items.name: Milestone repairs on the island
scope_items.desc: Structural, concrete, balcony and electrical work your engineer's recertification or milestone report calls for, built under permit and documented for the association's record.

faqs.q: There is an open permit on my Fisher Island residence from a previous owner. Now what?
faqs.a: It shows up in the permit search your buyer's title company runs, and lenders rarely fund past it. You do not need the original contractor. A licensed contractor can assume the file, pull the county record to see which inspections were never called, expose or test the work where that is required, correct whatever fails and carry it through to final sign-off. Begin the week you learn about it, not the week of closing.

faqs.q: Which office issues building permits for Fisher Island?
faqs.a: The county does. Fisher Island is unincorporated Miami-Dade, so applications go to the Department of Regulatory and Economic Resources instead of a city building department. That is only the public half of the approval. Before a crew steps off the boat you also need your building's sign-off on the alteration and contractor registration with the Fisher Island Community Association. We move the county file and the private approvals on parallel tracks, because handled one after another they add weeks nobody budgeted.

faqs.q: Can work that was already done without a permit be legalized now?
faqs.a: Usually, through an after-the-fact permit, though the standard is the same as if you had filed first. The county needs to see that what exists meets current code, which normally means drawings, certification by an engineer or architect, and product approval documents matching the units actually installed. Where glazing went in without a valid Notice of Acceptance, some of it may have to come back out. We tell you which of those two situations you are in before you spend on either.

faqs.q: Our building got a recertification or milestone inspection report. Can PGX do the repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The inspection itself belongs to your engineer or architect, and we keep that line clean rather than blur it. What we do is build what the report calls for: concrete restoration, balcony and railing work, waterproofing, electrical corrections, permitted through the county and documented so the association ends up with a clean file. On this island that also means barged materials, staged deliveries and residents who never moved out.

faqs.q: How long does permitting take, and what will it cost?
faqs.a: Weeks, not days, and the honest variables are the scope, the quality of the drawings, and how fast your association returns its approval. A file that goes in complete tends to draw one round of comments; a thin one draws three, and each round is another cycle. Fees are set by Miami-Dade County and scale with the declared value of the work, and we pass them through at cost. Any contractor quoting a firm number of days has not read the scope yet.

permitting-compliance.cta_sub: A permit number, a violation notice, an engineer's report, or drawings you simply want filed correctly. We will tell you what it takes — in English o en español.
